turns.message: There's a stretch of your life I don't have anything for yet, somewhere after the Mesa house. What were you doing for work back then?
I'd love to place the bike with no brakes properly. Where were you living when that happened?
The Mesa house puts it somewhere in that stretch. Was it before or after your brother arrived?
About five puts that somewhere around 1984, give or take a year — does that feel right?
Spring of 98, or is somewhere between 97 and 99 more honest?
Which of those two came first — the print shop, or the one out by the airport?
Work's gone quiet on that stretch, so let's try the other side of it — who was around the house then?
Spring of 1998, then, right before the move — that's a good place to leave it.
Was that before or after your sister was born?
Then let's leave it with her — it'll keep as long as you like.
Your timeline has that as 1998 and you're saying 1996 — I'd rather keep both than pick one. Which feels closer when you sit with it?
I want to build the spine of your timeline with you, and it starts in one place. When's your birthday?
Good — that anchors everything else. What's the first place you remember living?
Five to eleven in that house puts it at 1984 to 1990 — where did you go after it?
That's the spine — birthday, then the houses in order. Everything else will hang off it now.
That last part — standing in the doorway not knowing whether to go in — that's the whole thing, isn't it.
I want to put that where it belongs. Where were you living when it happened?
The Mesa house it is, then — I'll keep it in that stretch.
You were carrying that on your own the whole time. That's a lot to have held.
I've got the Mesa house already — that's enough to be going on with. Tell me what she said next.
Preschool-ish, then — somewhere in a couple of years rather than one day, or is it tighter than that?

Two things you've told me put the Dayton move in different places in time — the summer after your mother died, which was 1984, and being seven when you landed, which would be 1986. Both of them are still on the record. Which of those feels right to you?
The summer after your mother died, then. I'll let the other reading go and keep the record of you having said it.
That's alright. Both accounts can sit there — nothing about this has to be settled today, and I'll leave it exactly as you left it.
You've told me Harvey came into the world in 1948. Do you know the day, or is somewhere in that summer more honest?
